chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadhr, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A time will come upon people when they will complain to their Lord, Exalted and Glorious.' I asked: 'How do they complain to their Lord?' He said: 'A man will say, by God, I have not gained anything from such and such, and I do not eat or drink except from my principal capital. Woe to you! Is your principal capital and its peak not from your Lord, Exalted and Glorious?'
ai.seo_question: How do people complain to God according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on leases, this hadith highlights the spiritual danger of attributing financial success solely to one's own capital rather than divine providence. It serves as a critique of materialistic ingratitude, reminding believers that even their principal assets are ultimately gifts from Allah, thereby fostering a deeper sense of gratitude (shukr) in economic dealings.
